task.title: Publish the desktop app from this repository's releases
task.description:
Cut desktop builds from this repository, and retire the one they come from today.

Depends on CI: a release path that publishes what nothing verified is worse than no release path.

## Two numbers, with a cascade

Decided 2026-09-15.

- **The CLI keeps `vX.Y.Z`** and everything about its release path is unchanged.
- **The app has its own sequence**, tagged `desktop-vX.Y.Z`. A desktop release can be cut on its own whenever the app needs one; a desktop-only fix never bumps the CLI.
- **Every CLI release cascades.** When `vX.Y.Z` has published, `release.yml` cuts a companion desktop release automatically, bumping the app the same way the CLI was bumped (patch for patch, minor for minor). A CLI release therefore always reaches desktop users without anyone remembering to cut it.
- **The About panel shows both numbers**: the app's version and the version of the CLI it bundles.

## Which CLI a desktop build bundles

Never the working tree. The workflow builds the CLI at the newest `v*` tag reachable from the commit being released (`git describe --tags --match 'v*' --abbrev=0`), passed to `desktop/scripts/build-workbook.sh` as `WORKBOOK_REF`, and stamps it with that version the way `scripts/release.sh` does rather than with `git describe`. For a companion release that is the CLI just published. For a desktop-only release it is the last CLI release, so unreleased Go changes on `main` never ride along inside the app. `npm start` still builds the working tree.

## Where releases live

Each `desktop-vX.Y.Z` gets a permanent GitHub Release in this repository: macOS (arm64, x64; DMG and ZIP), Linux (x64, arm64; AppImage and deb), Windows (x64, arm64; NSIS), plus electron-builder's feed files (`latest-mac.yml`, `latest-linux.yml`, `latest.yml`). The same workflow then refreshes a rolling release tagged `desktop-latest` with the same assets, replacing what was there (`gh release upload --clobber`, moving the tag). Installer names carry no version (`Workbench-arm64.dmg`), so the rolling release's download URLs are stable and the site can link them.

Uploads go through `gh release`, the way `scripts/publish-release.sh` already works, not through electron-builder's publisher: the app's `build.publish` is the generic provider and only says where the app reads its feed.

## The update check

electron-updater's GitHub provider walks the repository's release feed and skips any tag that is not plain semver, so it cannot share a release list with the CLI: `desktop-v1.4.0` is invisible to it and `v0.6.0` carries no feed file. The app therefore uses the generic provider pointed at `https://github.com/dgoings/workbook/releases/download/desktop-latest`. The move already writes that into `package.json`.

The macOS behavior comes across unchanged. Those builds carry an ad-hoc signature rather than a Developer ID one, and Squirrel.Mac silently refuses to install over a bundle it cannot verify, so `quitAndInstall` returns having done nothing while the user believes they upgraded. The Mac path downloads the DMG and opens it in Finder instead. Windows uses electron-updater's native download-and-restart flow.

## Cutting a desktop release

The version is computed from the newest `desktop-v*` tag, the way `scripts/plan-release.sh` computes the CLI's from the newest `v*` tag, so that script grows a tag-prefix argument rather than a copy. Start with the Actions button (a `cut-desktop-release.yml` with the same bump/version inputs as `cut-release.yml`) and the cascade from `release.yml`; those cover every release the model needs. The tag is pushed and the desktop release workflow called directly, because a tag pushed with the default token starts no workflow. `release.yml`'s `v*` trigger does not match `desktop-v*`, and the desktop workflow's trigger must not match `v*`.

The workflow writes the tag's version into `desktop/package.json` before packaging (`npm version --no-git-tag-version`), so the checked-in `0.0.0` is never released.

`scripts/publish-release.sh` is untouched: desktop assets live in desktop releases, so its exact-asset-count check on rerun still holds.

## Signing

Ad-hoc signed and unnotarized on macOS, in `desktop/scripts/after-pack.js`, exactly as Workbench ships today; first launch needs right-click Open. Windows installers are signed through Azure Trusted Signing when the six repository secrets are present and are unsigned otherwise. Notarization is its own task.

## Last step

Archive `tylerkilgore/workbench` once a `desktop-v*` has been cut from here and verified to install. The one existing install is not migrated.
